skill.name: Hooks Automation
skill.description: Guides Claude Code hook automation with Claude Flow commands for task preparation, post-edit processing, session state, Git checks, MCP coordination, and memory workflows.
skill.summary: Configure Claude Code hooks for coordinated task, session, memory, and Git automation.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown formatting false positives from code fences and inline command examples. Confirmed risk remains for shell hook examples, production environment file handling, and unescaped runtime parameter interpolation in command hooks.

remediation.issue: Runtime values are interpolated into shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use argument arrays or strict escaping for file paths, task text, search patterns, result identifiers, and session identifiers.

remediation.issue: The guide includes automatic shell and Git hook examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings to review commands, run them in a disposable repository first, and require confirmation for destructive or networked operations.

remediation.issue: The guide references production environment files in hook examples.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid backing up, logging, or processing secret environment files by default. Require manual approval and redact secret paths in examples.

content.value_statement: Manual hook setup can be inconsistent across Claude Code projects. This skill guides automated hook configuration for tasks, sessions, memory, and Git workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains pre-operation and post-operation Claude Flow hook commands.
Shows Claude Code settings examples for tool, task, and session hooks.
Describes memory coordination patterns for multi-agent workflows.
Provides Git hook examples for commit, push, and quality checks.
Documents troubleshooting steps for hook execution and performance issues.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow CLI and compatible Claude Code hook support.
Does not install or verify hooks without user-approved local commands.
Command examples need local review before use in sensitive repositories.
MCP behavior depends on configured servers and available permissions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Hooks
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable hook plan for formatting, validation, and session state in one repository.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Use task and memory hooks to keep multi-agent Claude Code work aligned across sessions.

use_cases.title: Add Git Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Adapt the documented Git hook patterns for pre-commit checks, post-commit metrics, and push validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan basic Claude Code hooks for this repository. Focus on pre-edit validation, post-edit formatting, and session summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review Hook Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Claude Code hook settings for safety, missing timeouts, and unnecessary command execution. Suggest a safer configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Design Agent Coordination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hook workflow that coordinates backend, frontend, and test agents with memory keys and session restore steps.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Git Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a hardened Git hook automation plan for commits and pushes. Include command review, secret protection, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: I need hooks for a small TypeScript service.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan covering pre-edit validation, post-edit formatting, test execution, and session-end summaries.

output_examples.input: My team wants multi-agent memory coordination.
output_examples.output: A workflow that assigns memory namespaces, stores task decisions, restores session context, and exports summary metrics.

output_examples.input: Check this hook plan before production use.
output_examples.output: A risk review that highlights shell command use, sensitive file handling, timeout settings, and required manual approvals.

best_practices: Review every shell command before enabling it in automatic hooks.
Add timeouts, manual approval, and clear failure behavior for risky operations.
Keep memory keys organized by project, session, task, and agent role.
anti_patterns: Do not run templated tool parameters in shell commands without escaping.
Do not allow hooks to copy or log secret environment files by default.
Do not enable broad automatic hooks before testing them in a disposable repository.

faq.question: Does this skill install Claude Flow hooks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and configurations that users must review and run in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the guidance to reason about hook plans, but local command execution still needs review.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Code?
faq.answer: The hook examples are written for Claude Code and Claude Flow. Other tools may need adaptation.

faq.question: Is it safe for repositories with secrets?
faq.answer: Use caution. The examples mention environment files, so secret files should require manual approval and no logging.

faq.question: What should I review before enabling a hook?
faq.answer: Review shell commands, interpolated parameters, file access, timeouts, and whether failures should block the workflow.

faq.question: Can the skill coordinate multiple agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes task hooks, memory keys, session restore, and MCP coordination for multi-agent workflows.
